additional_info.subject: 0419080 - ID0414855-DC/Si-D/FR-[MP / R8 170002501] can see errors on this charger (C1) CRM:00314000160
additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Florent,
My name is Fosco, I am reaching out from the Expert Services team in regards of child case
0419080
. The ticket was opened to explain the new error messages observed on your end.
First of all, everything is working as intended. With the latest FW version of Sicharge D v6.1.3,
new OCPP Vender Error Codes were introduced
. These vendor codes are intended to provide more information to the Backend in terms of charger's behavior, but they are not referring to new errors per se, simply they were not reported to the Backend.
In details:
The VendorErrorCode “
secc pilot is E
” just refers to the fact that the pilot state of one outlet changed to E. This vendor code is usually sent to the Backend when a attempted charging session fails, or if a charging session fails, hence the pilot state is E. This message is also sent during the booting phase or converter grouping phase.
The VendorErrorCode “
modbus0 is not connected
” refers to a loss of communication to the SECC for 750ms. This event has no impact on the performance of the charger, even during a charging session. Only in rare case it could lead to outlets being unavailable for several seconds or interrupt a charging session.
The VendorErrorCode “
secc is offline
” refers to the happening of the coap polling error, an internal communication to SECC lost for a small interval of time. The OpenController will reconnect to the SECC within 5 seconds. Also in this case, this event has no impact on the charger, even during charging session.
In case these losses of communication appear more and more often, we could install a Hotfix on the SECC of the charger, which includes hardening patches regarding Coap communication and a Modbus reconnection hardening.
Furthermore, R&D team is planning, for the next FW release, to reduce the spamming of these error messages when they have no effect on the charger in terms of outlet unavailability.
As explained above, these are not new errors introduced by the new FW v6.1.3, but just new messages sent to the Backend. Unfortunately, we missed a proper communication to the CPOs in regards of the introduction of these new error messages. We apologize for that and we will communicate future new vendor codes within the Release Notes and Software Manual.
In case you have further questions, please do not hesitate to reply to this email.
Looking forward to hearing your feedback soon
With kind regards,
